paper.title: PAC-Bayesian Lifelong Learning For Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Lifelong multi-armed bandits (tasks sampled i.i.d. from a task environment)
unmapped: Lifelong / meta-learning: a sequence of n MAB tasks, each with m rounds, tasks drawn i.i.d. from an unknown task environment
Objective is a PAC-Bayesian lower bound on the marginal transfer reward (expected average reward over first m rounds of a new task using a prior drawn from a hyperposterior), not regret
Assumption (1): expected reward of later tasks is no smaller than earlier tasks for any prior
settings.definition_quote: We represent a multi-armed bandit (MAB) task as a couple T_i = (\mathcal{A}, \rho_i), where \mathcal{A} is a finite set of actions and \rho_i(r|a) is a distribution over rewards r that is conditioned on the action a. We assume that rewards are always between 0 and 1 and that tasks are sampled i.i.d. from an environment \mathcal{T}.

bound.expression: (1/lambda_1 + 1/(n_tasks*lambda_2))*KL_hyper + KL_base/(n_tasks*m_steps*lambda_2) + c_n + lambda_1/(8*n_tasks) + lambda_2*(E - 2)/(b_min*m_steps) + log(2/delta)/lambda_1 + log(2*m_steps/delta)/(n_tasks*lambda_2)

symbols.m_steps: number of rounds per task m
symbols.KL_hyper: KL divergence between hyperposterior and hyperprior
symbols.c_n: non-computable term measuring dependence of task rewards on previous tasks' data
symbols.b_min: minimum behaviour-policy probability over all tasks, rounds and actions

conditions: condition (1): expected reward for any prior is non-decreasing across tasks

source.label: thm:big_bound_bern
source.quote: If condition (1) is satisfied, then for any hyperprior P, any lambda_1 > 0, any lambda_2 in [0, m b_min] and any delta in (0,1], inequality holds with probability at least 1 - delta ... R(Q) >= hat R(Q) - (1/lambda_1 + 1/(n lambda_2)) KL(Q||P) - 1/(nm lambda_2) E[sum sum KL(A(D_i^{:j-1},P)||P)] - c_n - lambda_1/(8n) - lambda_2(e-2)/(b_min m) - (1/lambda_1) ln(2/delta) - 1/(n lambda_2) ln(2m/delta)

results.notes: Recorded as an upper bound on the deficit hat R(Q) - R(Q) (empirical multi-task reward minus marginal transfer reward), holding simultaneously for all hyperposteriors Q. This is a PAC-Bayesian generalisation bound, not a regret bound. Combines Lemma 3 and Lemma 6. With lambda_1 ~ sqrt(n), lambda_2 ~ sqrt(m), the paper says the gap is O(1/sqrt(n) + 1/sqrt(m) + ...), ignoring c_n.

bound.expression: (1/lambda_1 + 1/(n_tasks*lambda_2))*KL_hyper + KL_base/(n_tasks*m_steps*lambda_2) + c_n + lambda_1/(8*n_tasks) + lambda_2*(1 + tau)**2/(8*m_steps) + log(2/delta)/lambda_1 + log(2*m_steps/delta)/(n_tasks*lambda_2)

symbols.m_steps: number of rounds per task m
symbols.tau: importance-weight clipping parameter, weights clipped to [0, 1+tau]
symbols.KL_hyper: KL divergence between hyperposterior and hyperprior
symbols.c_n: non-computable term measuring dependence of task rewards on previous tasks' data

conditions: condition (1): expected reward for any prior is non-decreasing across tasks

R(Q) >= hat R_tau(Q) - (1/lambda_1 + 1/(n lambda_2)) KL(Q||P) - ... - c_n - lambda_1/(8n) - lambda_2(1+tau)^2/(8m) - (1/lambda_1) ln(2/delta) - 1/(n lambda_2) ln(2m/delta)

results.notes: Recorded as an upper bound on hat R_tau(Q) - R(Q) (clipped empirical multi-task reward minus marginal transfer reward), uniformly over hyperposteriors. Combines Lemma 3 and Lemma 8. Not a regret bound.

cited_results.cited_title: PAC-Bayes-Bernstein inequality for martingales and its application to multiarmed bandits
cited_results.setting_description: Single stochastic MAB with rewards in [0,1], adaptive behaviour policies bounded below by eps_m; PAC-Bayes-Bernstein bound on R_hat(Q_m) - R(Q_m), uniformly over Q_m and m, w.p. >= 1-delta
